## Methods {-}

### Population Dynamics {-}

For population $s$, the number-at-age $a$ that survived ($N_{S,s,a,t+\delta}$), were harvested from the fishery ($N_{H,s,a,t+\delta}$), and died from natural mortality ($N_{D,s,a,t+\delta}$) over the time interval $\delta$ are given by: 

\setcounter{equation}{0}
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
N_{S,s,a,t+\delta} &= N_{s,a,t} S(s,a,\delta) = N_{s,a,t} e^{-Z_{s,a}\delta} \\
N_{H,s,a,t+\delta} &= N_{s,a,t} H(s,a,\delta) = N_{s,a,t} \frac{F_{s,a}}{Z_{s,a}}\left(1 - e^{-Z_{s,a}\delta}\right) \\
N_{D,s,a,t+\delta} &= N_{s,a,t} D(s,a,\delta) = N_{s,a,t} \frac{M_{s,a}}{Z_{s,a}}\left(1 - e^{-Z_{s,a}\delta}\right)
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

where $N_{s,a,t}$ is the number-at-age $a$ at time $t$ for population $s$; $S$, $H$, and $D$ represent the proportions (fractions) of individuals that survived, were harvested, or died from natural mortality, respectively, over the time interval $\delta$; $F_{t,a}$ and $M_{t,a}$ denote instantaneous rates of fishing mortality and natural mortality at age $a$ and time $t$, and $Z_{s,a}$ denotes total mortality rate, where $Z_{s,a} = F_{s,a} + M_{s,a}$.

The probability transition matrix, when there is movement between regions, can be generalized as:

\begin{equation}
\mathbf{P}_{s,a,t,\delta} = \begin{bmatrix}
 \mathbf{O}(s,a,\delta) & \mathbf{H}(s,a,\delta) & \mathbf{D}(s,a,\delta) \\
 0 & \mathbf{I}_{H} & 0 \\
 0 & 0 & \mathbf{I}_{D}
\end{bmatrix}
\end{equation}

where $\mathbf{O}$ is the $n_R \times n_R$ matrix representing the combined probability of survival and movement between regions. Assuming movement occurs sequentially after survival, $\mathbf{O}$ is the product of the survival probability matrix ($\mathbf{S}$) and movement probability matrix $\mu$, such that $\mathbf{O} = \mathbf{S} \mu$. $\mathbf{H}$ is the $n_R \times n_F$ matrix representing proportions of individuals harvested by each fleet in each region, $\mathbf{D}$ is the $n_R \times n_R$ matrix representing proportions of individuals that died from natural mortality within each region, and $\mathbf{I}_{H}$ and $\mathbf{I}_{D}$, which have the same dimensions as $\mathbf{H}$ and $\mathbf{D}$), are identity matrices that ensure the overall dimensions of the probability transition matrix remain consistent when combined. If there is only one region and one fleet, these identity matrices reduce to scalars of 1.

For population $s$, the total number-at-age $a$ at the end of time interval $\delta$ can be generalized as:

\begin{equation}
\mathbf{N}_{s,a,t+\delta} = \mathbf{P}(s,a,\delta)' \mathbf{N}_{s,a,t}
\end{equation}

where the numbers of individuals that survived, were harvested, and died from natural mortality are decomposed as:

\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{N}_{S,s,a,t+\delta} &= \mathbf{O}(s,a,\delta)' \mathbf{N}_{s,a,t} \\
\mathbf{N}_{H,s,a,t+\delta} &= \mathbf{H}(s,a,\delta)' \mathbf{N}_{s,a,t} \\
\mathbf{N}_{D,s,a,t+\delta} &= \mathbf{D}(s,a,\delta)' \mathbf{N}_{s,a,t}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

### Population Structure and Seasonality {-}

A natal homing population structure is assumed in WHAM. Each population is associated with a natal region, and all fish originating in that  region must return there for spawning. Outside of the spawning season, fish can move between regions (see details in the sections on OM or EM movement dynamics). Seasonality is included to support the assumption of natal homing. Specifically, a number of time intervals within a year ($\Sigma_{i=1}^{n} \delta_i = 1$) are used to indicate movement dynamics prior to the spawning season, during the spawning season, and after the spawning season. The probability transition matrix for the entire year is a product of all "seasonal" matrices:

\begin{equation}
\mathbf{P}_{s,a,y} = \prod^{n}_{t=1} \mathbf{P}_{s,a,y,t}
\end{equation}

### Fishing Mortality ($F$) {-}

${F}$ at age ${a}$ for fleet ${f}$ is calculated as a product of fully selected ${F}$ and selectivity-at-age (i.e., the separability assumption) for fleet ${f}$: $\tilde F_{f,a} = \tilde F \textit{Sel}_{f,a}$. In WHAM, a fully selected, total ${F}$ is the maximum of the total ${F}$-at-age summed across all fleets:

\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
F_{\text{total},a,y} &= \sum_{i=1}^{n_f} F_{f_i,a,y} \\
F_{\text{total},y} &= \operatorname*{argmax}_a F_{\text{total},a,y} \\
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

### Reference Points {-}

The fully selected total $F$ defined above was used to estimate a single universal ${F}$ reference point applicable to all populations and regions. A 'static' SPR-based reference point was calculated by averaging all of the inputs (e.g., selectivity, natural mortality, movement, weight-at-age, maturity-at-age) over the most recent 5 model years for each region, except for recruitment, which was averaged over all model years for each region. 

For $X\%$ SPR-based reference points, WHAM uses a Newton method to solve for the universal $F_{X\%}$ reference point:

\begin{equation}
\tilde{F}^{(i)} = \tilde{F}^{(i-1)} - \frac{g\left(\tilde{F}^{(i-1)}\right)}{\tilde{F}^{(i-1)}g'\left(\tilde{F}^{(i-1)}\right)}
\end{equation}

where $g(F)$ is the difference between the weighted spawning biomass per recruit at $F$ and $X\%$ of the weighted unfished spawning biomass per recruit:

\begin{equation}
g(F) = \sum_{s=1}^S w_s \left( \frac{\tilde{\tilde{SSB}}}{\tilde{R}(F)} - \frac{X}{100} \frac{\tilde{\tilde{SSB}}}{\tilde{R}(F=0)} \right)
\end{equation}

Here weights are determined by the average recruitment for different regions/populations:

\begin{equation}
w_i = \frac{\bar{R}_i}{\sum_{i=1}^{n_s} \bar{R}_i}
\end{equation}

The fully selected total $F$ reference point can be disaggregated to regional $F$ reference points, given the relative contribution of selectivity ($Sel$) at age $a$ from each fleet in each region $R$: 

\begin{equation}
F_{X\%_{\text{a},R}} = F_{X\%} \text{$Sel$}_{a,R}
\end{equation}

The regional $F_{X\%}$ (e.g., $F_{40\%}$) does not guarantee achieving 40% of region-specific SPR, but serve to collectively achieve 40% of SPR at the global scale. Regional $F$ reference points are not currently implemented, as a unique solution is not guaranteed in the presence of movement between regions. An analogous Newton method is used to solve for $F$ that maximizes yield for MSY-based reference points.
